firstDiff: Language policies can shape which parts of a learner's repertoire become available during a task. In a Malaysian Grade 5 English-language classroom with an English-only policy, students used translanguaging during peer collaboration while encountering constraints from classroom expectations and the attitudes of others (Rajendram, 2023). A Canadian university study compared plurilingual and English-only instruction in an academic English programme and found greater development of plurilingual and pluricultural competence in the plurilingual group (Galante, 2022). Neither study measured secondary science understanding. Their relevance to my work lies in the language opportunities and constraints they document, rather than in evidence of science learning.

-

Gesture and shared modelling can make scientific relationships visible during an investigation, including relationships that a final written answer may not fully express. In a Swedish elementary science classroom, the language resources bilingual students used differed between teacher-led exchanges and small-group activities (Ünsal et al., 2018). An analytic framework distinguishes changes across representations from the ways learners combine words, gestures, and visual elements within a representation (Tang et al., 2014). In an out-of-school inquiry into electric flow and resistance, elementary-aged emergent bilingual students drew on linguistic and nonlinguistic resources as they developed models with peers and their instructor (Suárez, 2020). The study also describes how the instructor's pedagogical moves signalled when and how students could draw on those resources.

In an out-of-school inquiry into electric flow and resistance, emergent bilingual students drew on linguistic and nonlinguistic resources as they developed models with peers and their instructor (Suárez, 2020). The study also describes how the instructor's pedagogical moves signalled when and how students could draw on those resources.

Interpreting students' ideas across talk, writing, and images raises a methodological question about which records to preserve. Research on plurilingual identity texts has examined conversations alongside students' written and visual work (Prasad, 2015). A relational account of multiliteracies considers how meaning develops within social and cultural relationships (Simon, 2011). The literacy settings differ from those of secondary science. The same attention to conversations and classroom relationships may help me interpret written and visual work in science.
